claims.text: Gush Emunim was formally founded at Kfar Etzion at the beginning of 1974, its ideology rooted in the teachings of Rabbi Zvi Yehuda Kook; its first attempts at Sebastia were removed by the army seven times, and after the eighth they were permitted to settle in the army camp at Kaddum; Amanah was its settlement arm; after Likud came to power in 1977 it presented an 'emergency' settlement plan; its October 1978 blueprint resembled plans by Matityahu Drobles of the Jewish Agency's settlement department and agriculture minister Ariel Sharon.

In the Elon Moreh case (HCJ 390/79, 1979) the Supreme Court held the requisition of private land unlawful under Article 52 of the Hague Regulations because political and ideological considerations, including Gush Emunim pressure, were dominant over military need, and a military administration cannot create facts intended to outlast military rule.

After Elon Moreh the authorities relied on a stringent interpretation of the 1858 Ottoman Land Code to declare 'state land': 908,000 dunams in 1979–1992, which B'Tselem says amounted to more than 900,000 dunams, about 16% of the West Bank; Israel treats such land as state land an occupier may administer 'in trust'.

On 2 June 1980 car bombs planted by Israeli settlers maimed Nablus mayor Bassam Shakaa (who lost both legs) and Ramallah mayor Karim Khalaf (who lost a leg); a bomb meant for the al-Bireh mayor blinded a Druze police sapper; in 1984 IDF officers were charged; Ira Rappaport, convicted of membership in a terrorist organisation, was pardoned by President Herzog and released in 1988.

In July 1985 three settlers were convicted of murder for the 1983 attack on the Islamic College in Hebron (3 students killed, 33 wounded) and 12 others of crimes from firearms possession to manslaughter and conspiracy; nine were convicted over the 1980 mayor bombings; some were found guilty of planning to blow up the Dome of the Rock; settlement leaders sought a pardon from President Herzog, supported by many Likud ministers.

The Civil Administration was established in 1981 by Military Order 947 to carry out bureaucratic functions in the territories; it falls under COGAT in the Defence Ministry; it handles entry, travel and work permits and decides on approval of housing units in settlements.
